entry.summary: Visa-free short stays as part of the Schengen area.
entry.max_stay: 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area. Austria also has a bilateral visa-free agreement with Australia: confirm how it applies with the Austrian Embassy Canberra.
entry.pre_arrival: None today. ETIAS is on the watch list.
entry.other: Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo are taken at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do before arrival). Carry your passport when crossing borders inside Schengen.
entry.next_check: Read the Austrian Embassy Canberra's page on the bilateral agreement (its old address now returns 404).

tourism.detail: Australians are generally visa-exempt for short Schengen visits.
tourism.next: Check the Austrian mission and the full Schengen itinerary before departure.

meetings.detail: Meetings, negotiations and trade-fair attendance can fit a visitor trip when no Austrian work is performed.
meetings.next: Carry the invitation, schedule and business evidence.

conference.detail: Attending is distinct from delivering a paid or hands-on programme.
conference.next: Ask the host to classify any speaking, teaching or production role.

unpaid-speaking.route: Host classification; invited teaching/lecturing may have narrow rules
unpaid-speaking.detail: Unpaid cultural or academic activity still needs an Austrian work-law check; the settlement permit for artists is a longer route, not a same-day exemption.
unpaid-speaking.next: Have the institution or promoter obtain written classification.

paid-speaking.route: Austrian work authorisation, Red-White-Red or employer permit
paid-speaking.detail: Paid speaking, consulting and training can be employment or self-employment and must be matched to the work category.
paid-speaking.next: Let the Austrian engager choose the short assignment or residence route.

book-launch.detail: Rights meetings can be business; public readings, paid talks, signings and local retail need a host-led work/cultural classification.
book-launch.next: Separate literary appearance, publisher business, royalties and sales.

ai-teaching.detail: A university convention can support an academic visit; commercial AI training remains active work.
ai-teaching.next: Ask the institution to state the appointment, pay and duration.

remote-work.detail: Austria offers residence permits and Red-White-Red categories but no universal remote-worker visa; tax and residence remain distinct.
remote-work.next: Confirm the intended base and foreign-employer arrangement before relying on visitor entry.

entrepreneur.route: Red-White-Red Card startup founder or self-employed key worker
entrepreneur.detail: Austria lists startup founders and self-employed key workers; economic benefit, investment, jobs, know-how and qualifications matter.
entrepreneur.next: Prepare the business plan and evidence against the relevant Red-White-Red category.

trade.route: Short business visit; local operation requires Austrian status
trade.detail: Sourcing, meetings and fairs are visitor-friendly; local fulfilment, installation and sales may require work permission.
trade.next: Map the Austrian entity and physical delivery.

artist.route: Settlement Permit – Artists or event-specific work route
artist.detail: Austria publishes a settlement permit for artists covering self-employed or dependent artistic activity, with contract/evidence conditions.
artist.next: Have the promoter or employer specify the artistic contract and duration.

mixed-mission.route: Schengen visit plus Austrian host activation
mixed-mission.detail: The entry key is simple, while the activation key may be a Red-White-Red, artist, university or work route.
mixed-mission.next: Give the host one activity-by-activity brief.

filming.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (journalistic or media purposes)
filming.detail: Journalistic or media purposes are listed among visa-free purposes; paid production work and location permits are national matters.
filming.next: Ask the Embassy of Austria, Forrest about filming, and the local authority about locations.

research.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (short-term study or training)
research.detail: Short-term study and training are covered; paid research at an institution is paid activity.
research.next: Ask the Embassy of Austria, Forrest if the host pays you.

volunteering.detail: Volunteering isn't addressed in the EU guidance read.
volunteering.next: Ask the Embassy of Austria, Forrest.

laws.rule: Don't use or carry illegal drugs. Penalties for drug offences are severe. Possessing even small amounts of illegal drugs can lead to prison sentences.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: You must always carry ID, such as your passport. You may be asked to produce it by local police. Visitors are required to register with the police for stays longer than 3 days. If you're in public places or buildings, it's illegal to cover your face with clothing or objects so you can't be recognised. You may be fined or have to attend a police station if: you refuse to uncover your face when asked it's not possible to confirm your identity
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: For specific information on Bringing Medication into Austria (Austrian Federal Ministry for Social Affairs, Health, Care and Consumer Protection).

laws.rule: You can drive for up to 6 months with your valid Australian driver’s licence (digital driver's licences may not be accepted). You must also have either: an International Driving Permit (IDP), or a German translation of your licence
laws.heading: Driving permit

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Austria's currency is the Euro (EUR). Only change money at banks or other authorised dealers or withdraw cash from ATMs. Credit and debit cards are widely accepted, but some businesses may only accept cash. Declare funds of more than 10,000 euros or equivalent if you're travelling between Austria and a non-EU country. This covers all forms of currency, not just cash. Failure to do so will result in fines. You don't need to declare cash if you're travelling to or from another EU country.
